I will keep my planting simple and steady, because I am at the start of the season and I want crops that fit Quzhou County’s usual climate, my work capacity, and the land conditions in Hebei. I will mainly follow the common wheat-maize rotation, because that is the most reliable way for me to use the land through the full year, keep grain coming in, and spread risk across two seasons. I will plant winter wheat on all my land first, then after wheat harvest I will plant summer maize. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, stronger disease resistance, and better yield than old saved seed. I will not push fertilizer blindly; I will use moderate nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium together so the crop grows evenly and does not lodge too easily. I will irrigate a few key times instead of too many times, because water and labor both matter. I will also keep pesticide use limited to necessary control for weeds, insects, and disease, because I want to protect yield but avoid wasting money. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and common for preparing the field after each season.
